chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Muhammad al-Ansari, from Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir ibn Yazeed, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the midwife, is it permissible for the newborn to marry her? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No, and nor her daughter. She is one of his mothers.' And in the narration of Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), he said: 'If she was a midwife and moved on, then the midwives are many from that, and if she was a midwife and nourished, she is prohibited to him.'

key_terms.أُمَّهَات: Mothers (plural of umm, used here in the sense of kinship through birth/nourishment)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to marry the midwife who delivered you?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the prohibition of marrying the midwife by classifying her as a 'mother' through *radāʿ* (nourishment), a concept central to Shia jurisprudence where physical care creates kinship ties similar to blood relations. The narration distinguishes between a midwife who merely assists in delivery versus one who stays to nurse the child, with the latter incurring a permanent marital prohibition (*mahramiyyah*). This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the social and biological bonds formed through nurturing, extending the Quranic definition of mahram relatives to include those who provide essential sustenance.
